Article Title: SIM card rules 2026: What changes from August 24 and how many connections can you have
Article Text:
Govt has directed the telecos to strictly enforce the rule of not issuing a new connection to any subscriber already having nine SIMs (representative image)

How the new SIM verification system will work

How many mobile connections can you have?

Most of India: Maximum 9 mobile connections

Jammu and Kashmir: Maximum 6

Assam: Maximum 6

North-East: Maximum 6

When will the new system become fully real-time?

The government has directed telecom service providers to stop individuals from obtaining mobile connections beyond the prescribed limit of nine, with a new system coming into effect from August 24.Under the Department of Telecommunications (DoT) instructions, telecom companies will have to identify subscribers who seek a new mobile connection after already reaching the maximum number allowed in their name and inform them that another connection cannot be provided.The move will initially operate on a post-facto basis, allowing telecom operators to carry out the verification one day after a connection is enrolled.However, the government has asked operators to shift to a real-time system for identifying and preventing excess connections by November 30.From August 24, telecom operators will have to take technical and organisational measures to identify subscribers attempting to obtain connections beyond the prescribed limit.The DoT circular said: “From 24.8.2026 onward, TSPs shall take appropriate technical and organisational measures to identify each subscriber who seeks to obtain mobile connections beyond the prescribed limit using the representative image of the photo of a subscriber....andcommunicate to him that he already has maximum number of mobile connections permitted to an individual and accordingly, a new mobile connection cannot be provided to him. ”To help operators carry out these checks, the DoT will make available on the Digital Intelligence Platform (DIP) from August 23 a representative image of the photograph of every subscriber who has already reached the prescribed limit.Telecom companies will have to download these images daily and use them to identify subscribers attempting to obtain additional mobile connections.Until the system is fully implemented on a post-facto basis, any connection activated beyond the permitted limit during a day will have to be immediately suspended until the issue is resolved.Under existing DoT instructions issued on August 9, 2012, an individual can hold a maximum of nine mobile connections in their name across all telecom operators and licensed service areas in India.However, a lower limit applies in certain regions:Customers are also required to provide a declaration in the Customer Application Form (CAF) stating the mobile connections already held in their name across telecom operators and licensed service areas.The government has set August 24 as the date from which telecom operators must begin identifying subscribers trying to obtain connections beyond the permitted limit.The initial system can operate on a post-facto basis, but telecom operators have been directed to integrate the checks into the enrolment and activation process in real time by November 30.The respective Licensed Service Areas (LSAs) will be the competent authorities to decide issues arising from implementation of the instructions.The DoT has directed telecom operators to decline new connections to subscribers who already have the maximum number of permitted SIM cards.
Article Summary: Govt has directed the telecos to strictly enforce the rule of not issuing a new connection to any subscriber already having nine sims. The move will initially operate on a post-facto basis, allowing telecom operators to carry out the verification one day after a connection is enrolled.

Article Title: Crowd-funded anti-bribery portal shuts after amassing 2 lakh users in 48 hours
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Bribes.fyi began as a side project and, within 48 hours, clocked 5 million requests and 2 lakh new users. It shut down as suddenly as its meteoric rise took social media by surprise.Built by 20-year-old Delhi BTech student Aryan Nishad, it displayed a neon-red map of India for anonymous reports of alleged bribe demands. By Aug 17, it had logged reports from 253 cities—against police, RTOs, and revenue and land records offices, and passport offices. 37% were, interestingly, marked “refused”, meaning users said they did not pay and still got their work done. The site stressed these were user submissions, not verified cases.The site then abruptly went offline, citing traffic, data security, spam, duplicate entries and misuse. Calling the shutdown voluntary and precautionary, the team said: “What we did not build was the infrastructure to carry that kind of attention safely”. They acknowledged it was “not the right custodian for it at that scale”.In their farewell note, they said: "Shutting it down was our decision. It was always meant to send a signal, not point fingers.I think the signal was sent."The website and the traction it got from the public has generated huge conversation, with lawyers and experts weighing in. Section 8 of the Prevention of Corruption Act criminalises giving or promising an undue advantage to a public servant, punishable with up to seven years’ imprisonment after a 2018 amendment. An exception applies to someone compelled to pay who reports the demand within seven days. But a public admission on a website falls outside that protection.“So a person writing, ‘I paid Rs 5,000 to get my licence issued’ may be making a statement potentially relevant to their own criminal liability,” said Mishi Choudhary, technology lawyer and founder of Software Freedom Law Center (SFLC.in). The law has a policy problem, she said, and platforms must build “anonymity and security by design... from the beginning” and “not collect identity at all”.The safest approach, she said, is to collect minimum data because complainants “can’t be punished twice for doing what the system is forcing them to do”. Such a service is “a repository of sensitive personal data, allegations of criminal conduct and police information”, she added.The platform also raises intermediary-liability questions because it collected, moderated, categorised and mapped allegations instead of merely hosting them.“Safe harbour under Section 79 protects an intermediary that does not select or modify the information it hosts,” said Apar Gupta, founder director of Internet Freedom Foundation. “Moderating and approving reports... is an active function” that may exceed that role, he said, citing ongoing Wikipedia litigation in Delhi. Under Shreya Singhal vs Union of India 2015, removal requires a court order or govt notification, not a private complaint, though IT Rules prescribe grievance timelines. “A disclaimer offers no protection by itself.” Officials, he said, “complain to the police, not to the courts.”Platforms collecting names, phone numbers or IP addresses are data fiduciaries under the DPDP Act and face penalties up to Rs 250 crore for security failures, though Section 17 exempts govt agencies. “A platform cannot promise anonymity while retaining identifying records,” Gupta said. Data must be handed over within 72 hours of an authorised request, while disproportionate demands can be challenged under Puttaswamy.Yet “there is little protection for complainants”. Gupta cited a Lokniti-CSDS survey finding nearly two-thirds fear legal action for online speech. The Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014 was never operationalised.For a relaunch, Gupta recommended no accounts, no IP logs, stripped metadata, aggregate figures instead of names, referrals to newsrooms, a grievance officer and transparency reports. “Decentralisation is not a legal defence,” he said, noting BitChat and GitHub were blocked during July’s Delhi protests.
Article Summary: Bribes.fyi was built by 20-year-old delhi btech student aryan nishad. It displayed a neon-red map of india for anonymous reports of alleged bribe demands. Site then abruptly went offline, citing traffic, data security, spam, duplicate entries and misuse.

Article Title: Valkyrae’s AI controversy grows as streamer reveals the artist behind her disputed YouTube thumbnail
Article Text:
Valkyrae addresses AI allegations over YouTube thumbnail

Valkyrae defends thumbnail artist Anko

Rachell “Valkyrae” Hofstetter has addressed a growing debate over the artwork used for her YouTube livestreams after viewers accused her latest thumbnail of being AI-generated. The streamer defended her longtime thumbnail artist, Anko, while admitting she understands why some people reached that conclusion. Her comments also highlight a wider concern for digital artists as AI-generated content continues to reshape how audiences view online artwork.The controversy began after Anko, Valkyrae’s thumbnail artist, shared the creative process behind artwork for her Uncharted playthrough. The thumbnail initially received attention from viewers, but some quickly questioned whether artificial intelligence had been used to create it.That reaction eventually reached Valkyrae, who explained that Anko creates all of her YouTube livestream thumbnails and regularly shares his process online. She also pointed out the irony of the situation, saying that even those behind-the-scenes videos have not stopped people from making AI accusations.Valkyrae said:"Okay. We have to talk about this thumbnail debacle. I don't know what to do about this thumbnail debacle.So, as most of you know, every single one of my YouTube livestream thumbnails is made by the same artist. His name is Anko, and he makes all of them. He even posts on Twitter the art process of making them, but it still never beats the AI allegations. And the most recent thumbnail, he makes new thumbnails when I start a new game series, so, obviously, there is a new thumbnail for the Uncharted era. And people were saying, 'Oh, it's AI slop,' in the pre-chat."The streamer then offered a more nuanced response. Rather than dismissing viewers who suspected AI, she said she understood where their reaction came from. At the same time, she wanted to make clear that the artwork was not created using AI.Valkyrae added:"'Just ignore them.' Well, no. Okay? I don't blame people for thinking it's AI because AI is using people's art, like Anko's, to take over. But I would like to clear it up because there were a few people that were saying, 'Oh! When I saw the thumb, I also thought it was AI.' So now I am wondering how many people are out there that would watch the stream, but didn't because of the AI-looking thumbnail! But it's not AI."The discussion also became personal for Valkyrae because she said she felt bad for Anko. The thumbnail was later updated, with the artist adding his signature, giving viewers another indication of who created the work.Valkyrae explained that the situation made her think about the broader impact AI tools could have on working artists. For creators who depend on commissioned digital artwork, being mistaken for AI-generated work can create a difficult problem. The visual style that once helped an artist stand out can now cause audiences to question whether a human created it at all.She said:"I don't know, dude. I don't know what to do about it. I feel bad for him, though, because... and then, it, like, reminded me. I was like, 'Man, I just shouldn't do art thumbnails.' But then, the whole AI thing is doing what it does - making artists lose their jobs! Isn't that crazy?!"The controversy has now become more than a discussion about one YouTube thumbnail. Valkyrae’s response reflects a growing tension between AI-generated imagery and human-made digital art, particularly on social media where polished artwork can be judged within seconds.For Valkyrae, however, the message is straightforward: the Uncharted thumbnail was made by Anko, not AI. The debate instead shows how difficult it has become for artists to prove the human work behind their creations.
Article Summary: Valkyrae addresses ai allegations over youtube thumbnail. The streamer defended her longtime thumbnail artist, anko. Her comments highlight a wider concern for digital artists as ai-generated content continues to reshape how audiences view online artwork.

Article Title: Who is Gautam Rangarajan? Indian-origin strategist appointed to key role by UK PM Andy Burnham
Article Text:
Indian-origin strategist Gautam Rangarajan.

Who is Gautam Rangarajan ?

What will Gautam Rangarajan do at No. 10?

Burnham's government overhaul

British Prime Minister Andy Burnham has appointed Indian-origin strategist and former BBC executive Gautam Rangarajan as an Expert Adviser on Structure and Process in a newly created role at 10 Downing Street.Rangarajan, who brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media, is set to take up the position this week.Rangarajan is a senior strategist and media executive with more than two decades of experience across media, creative industries and public service broadcasting.Before his new government role, he spent more than 30 years at the BBC, beginning his career as a radio music producer and eventually rising to become the broadcaster's Group Director for Strategy and Performance.His experience includes developing strategy in rapidly changing markets, leading large-scale transformation initiatives and handling complex policy and financial negotiations.The exact details of Rangarajan's responsibilities are yet to be outlined. However, the UK PM's office said his appointment draws on his experience in corporate strategy and transformation.His role comes as Burnham undertakes a broader restructuring of the machinery of government, including the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.Rangarajan is expected to play a role in the planned transformation at the heart of the British government.Away from strategy and public service, Rangarajan also has a creative side. He describes himself as a professional choral singer and music producer, alongside his work in corporate strategy and organisational transformation.The appointment comes as Burnham reshapes his government following his recent rise to the role of Labour Party leader and Prime Minister.His administration has announced structural changes, including the launch of No. 10 North in Manchester and the creation of the Office for the Prime Minister and Cabinet.While the full scope of Rangarajan's new role remains unclear, his appointment places the former BBC executive at the centre of the UK government's planned transformation.
Article Summary: Indian-origin strategist gautam rangarajan appointed as expert adviser on structure and process at 10 downing street. He brings decades of experience in strategy, organisational transformation and media. The appointment comes as andy burnham reshapes his government following his recent rise to the role of labour party leader and pm.

A stressful situation seems lighter once someone finds a reason to laugh, and a serious problem often becomes easier to approach once it can be seen from another angle. It can create a little distance from fear, frustration and uncertainty, even when the circumstances themselves have not changed. Michael J. Fox , the actor and Parkinson's disease advocate, put a striking twist on that idea. "I think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor," he said. Not being able to laugh, in his framing, is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life, and coming from someone who has lived with a serious, lifelong illness for decades, the line carries a good deal more weight than a passing joke.This line comes from an interview Fox gave to journalist Amy Wallace, published on Reader's Digest's website. Fox is not really suggesting that a humourless person is dangerous in any literal sense. He is pointing at the seriousness that tends to surround someone who cannot laugh at themselves, cannot recognise irony, and cannot find any lightness in a genuinely difficult moment. Humour creates real distance from a problem.It lets someone acknowledge that something is hard without letting it completely take over.Life inevitably brings disappointment, uncertainty and real stress. Humour cannot solve every problem on its own, but it can genuinely change how someone responds to one. Being able to laugh during a hard period offers a small emotional break, and it can help people communicate when a direct, serious conversation feels too uncomfortable to actually have. None of this means every situation deserves to be treated as a joke. Humour and genuine seriousness can exist side by side.Stress tends to narrow someone's attention down entirely onto the immediate problem in front of them. A moment of real laughter can interrupt that cycle. Research into humour and stress has suggested that positive humour can genuinely influence mood and help people cope with stressful experiences, and laughter itself is linked to physiological changes, including a release of muscle tension. None of this should be overstated. Humour is never a substitute for professional help or a practical solution when someone faces a genuinely serious problem. As an everyday coping tool, though, it can offer a genuinely useful shift in perspective.One of the most valuable forms of humour is simply being able to laugh at your own missteps. Nobody gets everything right. People mispronounce words, misjudge situations and occasionally embarrass themselves, and someone who can acknowledge a mistake without being consumed by embarrassment tends to find it easier to actually learn from it. Self-directed humour also tends to make social interactions considerably more comfortable, since it signals that a person does not expect flawless perfection from either themselves or anyone else around them.Shared laughter helps people form real connections. Friends, colleagues and family members often use humour to build a sense of familiarity and trust, and a well-placed joke can break tension that a serious conversation might struggle to shift on its own. There is an important line here worth being clear about, between humour that actually brings people together and humour that humiliates someone else. Jokes built on cruelty or prejudice tend to damage relationships rather than genuinely strengthen them, and the most constructive kind of humour has never really needed anyone else to get hurt.Fox became one of the most recognisable actors of his generation through films and television, including Back to the Future and Family Ties. In 1991, at the age of 29, he was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease. He later made the diagnosis public and became a prominent advocate for Parkinson's research through the Michael J. Fox Foundation. His public approach to living with the condition has consistently included honesty, genuine optimism and humour, which gives his comments about laughter an extra dimension. His point was never that difficult experiences are inherently funny. It is that holding onto a sense of humour can help someone preserve real perspective while actually facing a genuine challenge. His decades-long relationship with humour, cultivated alongside a chronic illness he never chose, reveals that laughter was never a denial of hardship for Fox, but a deliberate, hard-won tool for maintaining perspective and genuine hope through real adversity.There is a meaningful difference between using humour to cope with something difficult and using it to avoid actually dealing with it at all. Some problems genuinely require serious attention and real action, and nobody can simply laugh away financial difficulty, illness or grief. What humour can offer instead is a small amount of emotional breathing space while someone continues addressing the actual underlying issue, which is really the whole distinction worth holding onto here.Fox's quote is deliberately provocative, and it should not be read as suggesting that serious people are inherently unpleasant. Some people naturally have quieter personalities, or simply express humour in a different way. The broader lesson is really about flexibility rather than personality type. Someone who can be genuinely serious when it matters, while still finding moments of humour elsewhere, tends to have more ways of responding to life's challenges than someone who treats every single situation with exactly the same level of weight.Humour is easy to underrate, since it can look insignificant next to more obviously serious qualities like intelligence or discipline. Even so, the ability to laugh genuinely shapes how people communicate, handle their own mistakes and respond to real difficulty. Fox's quote offers a deliberately provocative reminder that life does not always need to be approached with complete seriousness. There will be moments when humour is genuinely inappropriate, and problems that cannot be laughed away at all. In between those moments, though, holding onto a sense of humour tends to keep people connected, flexible and hopeful, which is really the whole point behind the line.
Article Summary: "i think the scariest person in the world is the person with no sense of humor" michael j. Fox, actor and parkinson's disease advocate. Not being able to laugh is not simply a personality quirk. It genuinely limits how someone can respond to life. Michael j. Fox was one of the most recognisable actors of his generation.

Article Title: Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra's 'reminder' to everyone investing in AI and calling it 'big': Right now, there is no AI without ...
Article Text:
Micron CEO feels AI is creating a more durable source

Demand outstripping supply

US chipmaker Micron reaches $1 trillion market capitalization

Micron CEO Sanjay Mehrotra recently said that artificial intelligence has fundamentally transformed the memory industry, long known for its boom-and-dust cycles. “Today there is no AI without memory. AI systems need more memory. They need higher performance memory. They need lower power memory,” Mehrotra told CNBC’s Jim Cramer on Mad Money. “So, the value of memory, that equation has totally changed.” His remarks came as Micron builds a vast semiconductor fabrication site near its Boise, Idaho headquarters, part of a planned $250 billion investment in U.S. manufacturing and research. The Boise complex will eventually house two fabs, each the size of 10 football fields, with the first expected to begin wafer production in mid‑2027.Mehrotra, who co‑founded SanDisk and has worked in chips for over 40 years, said AI is creating a more durable source of demand across data centers, autonomous vehicles, robots, and consumer devices. “Memory today is essential. That’s why I call it the strategic infrastructure of the AI era,” he said.Micron still cannot produce enough to meet demand. Mehrotra said data‑center customers want about 50% more supply than Micron can commit.The company has signed five‑year strategic agreements with 16 customers, with more added since its June earnings call, giving it greater visibility into long‑term demand. “All our customers across our end markets will buy everything that we make,” he said.In related news, recently, US chipmaker Micron Technology briefly crossed a market value of $1 trillion on May 26 as investor excitement around AI continued to drive demand for memory chips. According to a report by news agency Reuters, the sharp rally made Micron one of the biggest winners of the AI boom, with its shares rising more than 17% during trading. Micron’s stock jumped after brokerage UBS raised its price target on the company to $1,625 from $535, the report said. The company’s shares rose as much as 19.3% during the session before easing slightly later.As cited in the Reuters report, analysts say the surge reflects growing demand for advanced memory chips used in AI data centers and cloud infrastructure. The company’s rise also highlights how investors are now focusing beyond graphics chipmakers and looking at firms supplying key AI hardware components. “The need for pure memory has increased rapidly over very short periods of time, and clearly, Micron sits at the center of it,” Art Hogan, chief market strategist at B. Riley Wealth, told Reuters. “Today's crossing of the $1 trillion mark for Micron is just an exclamation point on the story of the massive amount of demand needed to run data centers in this AI revolution,” he added.
Article Summary: Micron ceo feels ai is creating a more durable source of demand across data centers, autonomous vehicles, robots, and consumer devices. Us chipmaker micron technology briefly crossed a market value of $1 trillion on may 26 as investor excitement around ai continued to drive demand for memory chips.

Article Title: Microsoft is hiring a legal engineer to teach lawyers across the company how to…
Article Text:
Microsoft wants a lawyer who can build AI agents, and it is paying up to $278,900 for one

Why Microsoft wants a lawyer who can also write software

The legal engineer job is spreading from startups to Big Tech

Microsoft has spent the past two years telling everyone else that AI is about to change how work gets done. Now it wants someone to prove the point inside its own legal department. The company has posted a job for a principal legal engineer, an unusual hybrid role that asks for a practising attorney who can also ship software, with base pay topping out at $278,900 a year.The listing, spotted on LinkedIn this week by Business Insider, puts the hire inside Microsoft's Customer & Partner Solutions group, the arm that supports the company's commercial business. The work is deliberately hands-on: building AI agents, sharpening prompts, and training attorneys and paralegals to actually use the tools. "This is a role for a builder," Microsoft wrote in the job description, adding that the person will partner directly with engineering rather than advise from the sidelines. Microsoft did not respond to Business Insider's request for comment.Lawyers were the corporate world's great tech holdouts for decades, understandably nervous about tools that could get one detail wrong in a 90-page agreement. That resistance is thinning. Clients are now pushing outside firms toward tools like Harvey and Claude for Legal to turn work around faster and bill less for it.The same pressure has moved in-house. Legal teams are betting that software can handle contract edits and policy drafting, letting them keep more of the early work and hand outside counsel matters that are already halfway done.Microsoft has a head start here because it builds some of these tools itself. Its lawyers already use Copilot for routine work, including contract review, where it compares a draft against similar agreements, flags issues and suggests edits that match company policy. Harvey is being rolled out across Corporate, External, and Legal Affairs.Until recently, legal engineer was mostly a startup title, filled by ex-lawyers with technical chops who sat close to customers. Palantir posted its own embedded legal engineer role last month, promising to turn manual workflows into automated ones.Microsoft wants a law degree and at least seven years of practice. Experience with Harvey or Copilot is preferred. Base pay starts at $147,000.
Article Summary: Microsoft wants a lawyer who can build ai agents, and it is paying up to $278,900 for one. The company has posted a job for a principal legal engineer, an unusual hybrid role that asks for a practising attorney who can also ship software. The work is deliberately hands-on: building ai agents and training attorneys and paralegals to use the tools.

Beats 360 may be offered in six colours

Beats 360 price and features

Article Title: IBM CEO Arvind Krishna on his letter that ‘shocked’ business world, sent company's stock over 25 percent down, making it 'worst day' in IBM history
Article Text:
IBM CEO Arvind Krishna

Why IBM CEO thinks it was important to ‘tell’ beforehand

Facing an impending quarterly earnings miss driven by shifting enterprise IT budgets and rising AI distractions, IBM Chairman and CEO Arvind Krishna opted for radical transparency -- a move that triggered a historic stock plunge but is reported to have aligned with his core leadership philosophy. In an interview with CRN, IBM CEO Krishna detailed the high-stakes decision to pre-announce the 115-year-old tech giant's financial shortfall eight days before its scheduled July 22 earnings call. The disclosure sent IBM shares tumbling more than 25%, marking one of the steepest single-day declines in the company's history.IBM's underperformance stemmed from enterprise clients pausing infrastructure projects to front-load spending on data center hardware amid supply constraints and surging costs. Additionally, Krishna noted that customer attention had been diverted by security debates surrounding an AI model released by Anthropic. He reduced IBM's expected full-year revenue growth for the year by more than $600 million, saying that the fall is in part due to some clients pushing out IBM infrastructure projects to pay for the growing cost of supply constrained memory, storage, servers and other data center infrastructure.Rather than holding the bad news for the standard earnings cycle, Krishna fell back on a long-standing operating principle: "If there’s a hard thing to be done, do it earlier rather than later," Krishna told CRN.By clearing the bad news early, Krishna aimed to pivot the official earnings call away from post-mortem explanations and toward strategic fixes. "Time will tell whether that was the right decision. I tend to think it was," Krishna said. "Otherwise, we would have been spending the last week explaining the hesitation as opposed to what we are going to do to go fix it."The decision highlights the pressures facing IBM as it balances heavy investments in generative AI and long-term quantum computing against Wall Street's short-term expectations. When asked by CRN about potential vulnerability to activist investors or board friction following the market reaction, the CEO, who took the helm in April 2020, remained pragmatic about corporate oversight."If you falter, one should always be just prepared is my view," Krishna said, adding that public CEOs must constantly evaluate whether they are delivering sufficient returns. "And activists, at the end, if I look at the good side, are trying to come in to say, 'I need better returns for clients and for investors.' And if that’s the goal, then one should be prepared to deal with them. That is just the nature of today’s world that we live in. "Krishna maintained that his primary strategy to protect the company's innovation roadmap remains centered on client satisfaction and workforce investment.IBM CEO Krishna reasoned the Q2 weakness to deal ‘deferral, and not destruction’. He said, “This was deferral and not destruction.” Krishna made the statement while talking to analysts during IBM’s latest quarterly earnings call with analysts. Krishna’s confidence comes in part from the fact that one-third of those largest infrastructure projects requiring a lot of customer CapEx have already closed.
Article Summary: Ibm chairman and ceo arvind krishna opted for radical transparency. The disclosure sent ibm shares tumbling more than 25%, marking one of the steepest single-day declines in the company's history. Krishna: "if there’s a hard thing to be done, do it earlier rather than later"

Article Title: A Chinese robot ‘dies’ after hitting safety wall during World Humanoid Robot Games running test
Article Text:
Chinese robot hits safety wall during running test

World Humanoid Robot Games set for 2026

Unitree unveils robot that is claimed to run faster than Usain Bolt

A bipedal Chinese humanoid robot allegedly training for World Humanoid Robot Games has gone viral after it lost control during a running test. In a viral video shared by X (formerly Twitter) user @pianhangx, the robot can be seen running toward the barrier before crashing into it, with its body bending sharply at the waist and sparks coming from the machine. The dramatic crash has led to social media users describing the incident as the moment the “robot dies.” The incident took place as robots prepare for the 2026 edition of the World Humanoid Robot Games in Beijing, China. The event kickstarts on August 22 and will showcase a record 2,056 robots and 666 teams this year.According to reports, the humanoid robot was taking part in a training session for the running competition when it appeared to lose control. In the video, it can be seen running at high speed and failing to stop before hitting the safety wall. The impact caused the robot's body to bend at the waist, while sparks could be seen coming from it.The video was shared on social media on August 20 and quickly attracted attention. At the time of writing, it has garnered over 13 million views. “The robot ran too fast to brake in time, crashed into the cushion, and broke its waist,” the Twitter user wrote.Times of India was not able to independently verify the viral video.The World Humanoid Robot Games first took place in Beijing in 2025. The event brings humanoid robots together for competitions based on sports and other activities. As mentioned above, the 2026 event is expected to be significantly larger, with 666 teams and more than 2,056 robots taking part across 50 events.The competition will include running and other sports, while robots will also take part in activities such as dance performances and serve as flag bearers.In another news, Chinese robotics firm Unitree has unveiled a new "Superman" humanoid robot that is claimed to outrun and outjump top human athletes. The company said the robot can reach a top speed of 12.66 meters per second (m/s) — faster than the roughly 12.4 m/s top speed achieved by Usain Bolt during his world-record 100m run in 2009.
Article Summary: Chinese robot hits safety wall during running test. Incident took place as robots prepare for the 2026 edition of the world humanoid robot games in beijing, china. The video was shared on social media on august 20 and quickly attracted attention. At the time of writing, it has garnered over 13 million views.

Article Title: Elon Musk’s Starlink seeks fresh India approval; says it will help ‘least served’...
Article Text:
What Elon Musk said about Starlink’s India launch

Starlink’s second attempt after an earlier rejection

Direct‑to‑device tech imminent

Regulatory and security challenges

Elon Musk’s Starlink has renewed efforts to launch satellite communication services in India. According to a report by Economic Times, the company is resubmitting an application to the Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN‑SPACe) for approval of its Gen 2 constellation. The new system would operate at altitudes of 340–615 km in low earth orbit and introduce direct‑to‑device (D2D) connectivity, a feature Musk has touted as critical for reaching underserved communities.Elon Musk underscored the importance of Starlink’s India push in a recent post on X, saying the service would help the “least served” communities. Replying to a post on X, Musk wrote, ‘Starlink would help the least served in India, especially in rural areas.’The Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (IN-SPACe) had rejected an earlier application from the Elon Musk-owned company for its planned 30,000-satellite internet constellation a few years ago, citing non-conformity in certain features and spectrum bands. According to a person familiar with the details, who spoke on condition of anonymity since the specifics aren't public, the company has now applied for authorisation of its Gen 2 constellation, which would operate at an altitude of 340-615 km in low earth orbit.Starlink, operated by SpaceX and the world's largest LEO satellite operator, remains bullish on India's satcom market, which industry watchers describe as still nascent but carrying significant long-term potential. The company had originally applied for both Gen 1 and Gen 2 constellations to begin services in India, but IN-SPACe approved only the Gen 1 constellation, comprising 4,408 LEO satellites offering traditional broadband services, in July 2025.India is considering opening more spectrum bands for satellite communications and allowing D2D features, prompting Starlink’s reapplication. If approved, the Gen 2 constellation could give Starlink a significant edge by enabling mobile connectivity directly to consumer devices, bypassing traditional telecom networks.So far, no non‑geostationary satellite operator — including Starlink, OneWeb, or Jio’s SES joint venture — has launched commercial services in India due to pending security clearances and spectrum allocation. The Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI) has issued pricing recommendations, but the government has yet to finalize rules. Telecom operators have warned that D2D services could threaten their business and have pushed for satellite firms to face the same regulatory obligations.
Article Summary: Starlink has renewed efforts to launch satellite communication services in india. The company is resubmitting an application to the indian national space promotion and authorisation centre (in‑space) for approval of its gen 2 constellation. The new system would operate at altitudes of 340–615 km in low earth orbit and introduce direct‑to‑device (d2d) connectivity.

Article Title: ChatGPT can now send texts for Mac users with new Apple Messages plug-in, but why they need to be careful about using this feature
Article Text:
What the new ChatGPT feature actually does

Why this could be a sensitive move for Apple

How OpenAI says it's handling privacy

What users actually have to enable

OpenAI has rolled out a new Apple Messages plug-in for its popular chatbot ChatGPT on Mac, enabling the AI system to read, write and send texts directly through iMessage. The integration also allows ChatGPT to search conversations and generate summaries, expanding its functionality beyond productivity apps like Notes and Xcode. OpenAI stressed that the feature requires explicit user consent and runs locally on the Mac, using AppleScript and Accessibility tools to interact with the Messages app. During setup, users encounter multiple opt‑in menus, including a permissions screen confirming that on‑device message history will be accessed.The new ChatGPT plug-in introduced by OpenAI will enable the chatbot to conduct direct actions within the Apple Messages app. ChatGPT will be able to read, wrote and also send text messages on the behalf of the user. Along with this, it will also be able to search through the existing messages and create summaries or also pull other information out of conversations, effectively giving ChatGPT hands-on access to a core piece of Apple's messaging ecosystem.According to a report by Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has built much of its brand identity around strong privacy protections, and the company has historically been especially protective of the contents of users' messages.A tool built by a third-party AI company, one capable of processing Apple customers' message data through OpenAI's own systems, is the kind of feature likely to draw scrutiny from privacy advocates and, potentially, from Apple itself. An Apple representative did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the launch.The timing adds another layer of tension: the feature arrives amid an already strained relationship between the two companies. Apple sued OpenAI last month, accusing the AI firm of stealing information related to upcoming Apple products.In response to questions about the new integration, OpenAI emphasised that the feature requires explicit user consent and does not build an index of a person's entire message history. The company said the plug-in runs locally on the Mac itself, relying on existing macOS tools such as AppleScript and Accessibility features to interact with the Messages app, rather than routing message data through a separate indexing system.Setting up the integration isn't a single toggle. When a user first configures it, ChatGPT displays a permissions screen explaining that the app will access the computer's on-device message history. Beyond that in-app consent step, users also need to adjust several privacy settings directly within the Mac's System Settings app, including enabling a feature called Full Disk Access. Users must additionally grant ChatGPT permission to access contact names and automation tools, a setup process similar to what's required to enable other AI-based automation software, such as Codex Computer Use.This isn't OpenAI's first foray into pulling personal data from Apple's ecosystem. The company recently added support for analyzing data from a user's iPhone or iPad Health app as well, though Apple's iOS and iPadOS include a built-in permission step specifically requiring users to approve sharing that health data with ChatGPT before it can proceed.
Article Summary: Openai has rolled out a new apple messages plug-in for its chatbot chatgpt on mac. It will enable the ai system to read, write and send texts directly through imessage. The integration also allows chatg pt to search conversations and generate summaries. Openai stressed that the feature requires explicit user consent and runs locally on the mac.

Article Title: Netflix unveils ‘VOID’, an AI model that can change a movie plot
Article Text:
Netflix

How Netflix VOID works







Netflix has unveiled an AI model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, Netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next, essentially altering the causality. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background. VOID goes a step further: after erasing an object from a scene, it calculates how the surrounding environment should realistically respond to its absence, and in the process it adjusts the behaviour of other elements in the frame accordingly.The model, called VOID, is a vision-language system designed to edit video footage with a level of contextual awareness that sets it apart from several existing tools.For example, imagine this scenario: A movie director has just wrapped up a multi-million dollar action sequence where the star drives straight into a fiery, head-on collision. The cars explode, debris scatters, and the scene is a wrap.But suddenly, there is request to change the scene: The character survives and drive off into the sunset instead. This would mean costly reshoots or millions spent on computer-generated graphics.Netflix’s VOID can alter the scene and digitally erase the collision, the second vehicle, the smoke, and the flying debris. It will then generate new, realistic footage of pristine pavement, making it look as though the main character simply drove down an empty, peaceful road.The AI’s ‘magic’ lies in its grasp of real-world physics. Let us understand this by a different example. If a video shows a person jumping into a pool and splashing water onto the deck, VOID can completely erase the person. It will then intelligently alter the water and the wet concrete, leaving behind a perfectly still, undisturbed pool as if nobody had ever jumped in.“To train the model, we generate a new paired dataset of counterfactual object removals using Kubric and HUMOTO, where removing an object requires altering downstream physical interactions. During inference, a vision-language model identifies regions of the scene affected by the removed object. These regions are then used to guide a video diffusion model that generates physically consistent counterfactual outcomes,” Netflix said.“Experiments on both synthetic and real data show that our approach better preserves consistent scene dynamics after object removal compared to prior video object removal methods,” the company added.Netflix isn’t keeping this powerful tool locked behind studio doors, and made the VOID model available to the public on the AI platform Hugging Face, allowing anyone to download and use it.While there are already several video-altering tools on the market, such as Runway, DiffuEraser, and ProPainter, the Netflix team claims VOID is vastly superior, as per The Register.
Article Summary: Netflix has unveiled an ai model that can alter the scene. While this is nothing new, netflix’s model not just remove objects from video, it understands what should happen next. Most object-removal technology leaves a gap where something used to be and/ or fills it with a plausible-looking background.

Article Title: AI data centers are causing 'stress' not just to tech companies, but also private insurers
Article Text:
Massive investments, growing risks



Unique challenges for data centre insurance companies





AI data centers are reportedly putting new pressure on the insurance industry. According to a CNBC report, experts warn that the rapid growth of these projects is becoming a “stress test” not just for tech companies, but also for private insurers and lenders. Consulting firm McKinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. As costs rise, tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects. The scale of investments is creating challenges for insurers.“When you put $10 to $20 billion plus in a single location, it creates capacity issues in the marketplace,” said Tom Harper, data center leader at insurance broker Gallagher as quoted in the CNBC report.He added that the sector has been a “real stress test” over the last few years, as insurers struggle to provide coverage for such large and complex projects. While these facilities are seen as high-quality assets, Harper said insuring them has become difficult due to their size and risk concentration.Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Companies including Nvidia, Microsoft and BlackRock have already taken part in large investment deals.Rajat Rana, partner at Quinn Emanuel Urquhart & Sullivan, described the scale as unprecedented. “We’re talking about trillions of dollars, and almost going back to the same cycle where there’s almost no transparency about the financing structures — the scale is astronomical,” he said. He added that the boom in AI data centers could be “the largest peacetime investment project in human history.”Experts say the way these projects are financed is adding another layer of risk. Much of the funding is happening through complex and less transparent debt structures. Rana warned that this trend feels like “deja vu,” referring to past financial cycles. He said the lack of transparency could create risks for investors, insurers and pension funds.As stated in the CNBC report, data centers offer unique challenges due to their mix of real estate and advanced technology. Insurers are now designing custom policies to manage these risks. However, challenges remain. Large facilities are often located in areas prone to extreme weather, and they store expensive equipment, sometimes even before installation.Another key concern is the mismatch between the lifespan of data centers and the hardware they use. While data centers can last decades, GPUs — the chips powering AI — typically last around seven years. Rana described this as a “GPU debt treadmill,” saying, “This is almost like a treadmill that these AI data centers are running on.”He explained that companies may need to keep raising debt to upgrade infrastructure as technology evolves.
Article Summary: Private data center deals have crossed $10 billion regularly, with some reaching as high as $40 billion. Mckinsey estimates that global spending on data centers could reach $7 trillion by 2030. Tech giants are increasingly relying on private equity, private credit and debt to fund these projects.
